about: What a model of [JEngine] will structurally be unable to predict, one record each: claim, mechanism, evidence, asserted_value, source. See felizjueves.literature.limits.

limits.claim: exact_given_inputs on jengine/table1 (FLOPs): no recovered set of inputs reproduces all 40 printed cells. The cut IS recovered (plan/recovery.py, two-ended nearest fill per direction, which also gives all 40 of Table 3); the sieve's inputs are not.
limits.mechanism: Table 1 is post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order: an order of a batch's targets, up to 969! of them at L = 16, one batch. [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says the order moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, and that the authors did not optimise it; they do not state the order they used. So the order is an unpublished input with no rule to recover it from, and the printed cells sit inside its spread. Also unpublished, and searched below: which other direction a re-parented child takes, how far the upward sweep deletes, and whether the walk is breadth- or depth-first.
limits.evidence: Every search below uses the recovered cut and the counting conventions #10 fixed (1/2/3 FLOPs per node by r_d; fundamentals with m > 0 are intermediates). (1) The literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order: 9/40 exact, (7,3) (7,6) (7,9) (8,6) (8,9) (9,6) (9,9) (10,9) (11,9). (2) The literal sieve over plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders (hermite_targets and its reverse; |r| ascending or descending, then the components in each of the 6 axis orders, all ascending or all descending): best 17/40 ('|r| asc, then xzy desc'). (3) A scratch variant of the sieve, not kept in the repo, over those 26 orders x 7 re-expansion choices (smallest r_d', largest r_d', xyz, zyx, smallest r_d' ties to z, cyclic successor, cyclic predecessor) x 2 sweeps (every orphaned node, or only i and its parents upward) x breadth- or depth-first x [r-1d] or [r-2d] enqueued first: 1456 configurations, best 17/40 Table 1 together with 29/40 Table 2. (4) Random seed orders, each sieved twice (smallest- and largest-r_d' re-expansion): 6000 runs (3000 orders) at (7,1) and at (8,1) reach the printed pair in 3578 and 460 of them, so those cells ARE seed-order effects; 600 runs (300 orders) at (16,1) never reach it (best FLOPs 5666 against the printed 5633; the hermite order gives 5644), so the paper's order there is in the tail, and no rule this search knows names it. Bounded at that point on purpose: the remaining space is the factorial order space itself, and searching it for each cell would be a per-cell fit.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the 31 cells above, under the recovered cut and the literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order; their printed values are taken from the table as published

limits.claim: exact_given_inputs on jengine/table2 (max intermediates per batch): no recovered set of inputs reproduces all 40 printed cells. The cut IS recovered (plan/recovery.py); the sieve's inputs are not.
limits.mechanism: Table 2 is post-sieve, as Table 1 is, and the intermediates the sieve deletes depend on the same unpublished seed order ([JEngine, v2, §4.1]: up to ~2%, not optimised, not stated). The record for jengine/table1 gives the full argument; the search was one search scoring both tables.
limits.evidence: Same search as jengine/table1's record. (1) Literal sieve, hermite_targets seed: 17/40 exact, (7,3) (7,6) (7,9) (8,6) (8,9) (9,6) (9,9) (10,6) (10,9) (11,6) (11,9) (12,6) (12,9) (13,9) (14,9) (15,3) (15,9). (2) Best of the 26 structured seed orders with the literal sieve: 29/40 ('hermite-reversed'; '|r| asc, then xzy desc' gives 28). (3) Best of the 1456 scratch-variant configurations: 29/40. (4) Random seed orders: the printed (7,1) and (8,1) cells are reached; the printed (16,1) cell is not in 600 runs (range 1633-1666 against the printed 1647, together with FLOPs never at 5633).

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the 23 cells above, under the recovered cut and the literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order; their printed values are taken from the table as published

limits.claim: at_or_under on the searched board, jengine/table1 (FLOPs) and jengine/table2 (max intermediates): 21 cells of Table 1 and 3 of Table 2 stay over the printed value under the searched plans. Table 3 is at or under in all 40. Every residual cell is over by at most +2.04%, and all but one by at most +1.04%.
limits.mechanism: The printed cells are post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order, which [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, was not optimised, and is not stated (the jengine/table1 exact_given_inputs record above has the full argument). The residual margins sit inside that spread: the paper's numbers are one draw from the seed-order space, and in these cells the draw is better than any order in the bounded family searched. Reaching it means searching the factorial order space per cell, which is a per-cell fit to the printed answer, not a generator choice. The one margin at the edge of the spread, (16, 1) Table 1 at +2.04%, is the objective's price: putting intermediates before FLOPs takes a seed order with 2 fewer intermediates and 104 more FLOPs; the literal hermite order is +0.20% there and the cell is over either way.
limits.evidence: plan/search.py, exhaustive per (L, n_batches) and recorded in data/scoreboards/jengine/searched_cuts.json. SEARCHED: every shared contiguous cut (C(L, k - 1), at most 120 per cell) crossed with plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders, at most 3120 full plans per cell (partition, MILD DAG per batch, sieve, PlanCost). OBJECTIVE, stated before scoring and not tuned to it: feasible if max targets <= the cell's minimax + 1 (the minimax tolerance), then fewest max intermediates, then fewest FLOPs; ties to the lowest cut, then seed_orders() order. RESULT: Table 1 21/40 over, Table 2 3/40, Table 3 0/40 (the first search, cut only and minimax tolerance 0, had 30, 13, 0 and a worst margin of +7.50% at (15, 9) Table 2; the tolerance closes that cell in all three tables). UNREACHABLE, independent of the objective: in every residual cell, NO candidate in the whole searched space -- any cut, any of the 26 orders, any number of targets -- is at or under the printed value in all three tables at once; in each the smallest FLOPs any feasible candidate reaches is still over Table 1. NOT SEARCHED: per-direction cuts, seed orders outside the structured family, the sieve's re-expansion choice and sweep (the jengine/table1 record above searched those against exact_given_inputs and stopped at 17/40), and no-sieve.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the cells above, with their margin in percent over the printed value; their printed values are taken from the tables as published
